title: Canary watchlist curation and comm-bonsai rollout dossier — 2026-03 (draft)
content:
Purpose and constraints:

This doc is a compact, tactical runbook for the upcoming canary window for the edge-routing + kv-cache changes (batching/kv-cache control flags). It focuses on:
- a small, curated watchlist of signals (the Bonsai watchlist) to detect early regressions in latency, cost-per-token, and tokenization regressions;
- an hourly cadence/launcher for the first 36 hours;
- a comms recipe for internal shifts (ops, SRE, product) and a minimal customer-facing blurb if needed;
- explicit rollback triggers and a short post-mortem template.

Why "comm-bonsai"? The idea is to keep the signal set small, sculpted, and fast to evaluate—like a bonsai garden: intentionally pruned metrics that surface badness quickly without noise.

Objectives (priority order):
1) Detect and roll back any user-visible latency regressions above 20% p50 or 15% p95 for high-throughput routes within 30 minutes of first signal.
2) Catch tokenization/formatting regressions that increase fallback rates or cause hallucination spikes (measured via eval prompt set A).
3) Ensure no sustained >10% increase in cost-per-token across sampled workstreams for 2 consecutive hours.
4) Validate KV cache hit-rate behavior (expected delta <= 3% from baseline); flag if hit-rate drops >5% sustained for 30m.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: hosted API routes: /v1/generate-high, /v1/chat-stream, and internal model routing tests.
- Non-goal: Large-scale traffic shaping experiments; we will not adjust global throttles during the canary except via documented safety lanes.

Preflight checklist (48–72h before deploy):
- [ ] Confirm canary cohort: 1% of traffic for 24h, rising to 5% at T+24h if stable.
- [ ] Bake a snapshot: runtime image tag runtime@sha256:3a7f-canary-2026-03 and store in release registry.
- [ ] Smoke test matrix: run generator/smoke-suite (smoke/generator/basic, smoke/chat/flow, smoke/embeddings/consistency) and attach logs to PR.
- [ ] Baseline telemetry snapshot: export last 7d p50/p95 latency, cost-per-token, KV hit-rate, fallback-rate for the target routes (save to S3 path: s3://redwood-rollouts/baselines/2026-03-canary.json).
- [ ] Notify policy: post to #release-ops, #sre, and product release Slack channels with rollout schedule and pager roster.
- [ ] Confirm on-call coverage: primary SRE (Daniel Kim), backup (Marta Lopez), runtime owner (Aisha Patel).
- [ ] Confirm canary termination automation is in staging: auto-rollback lambda is enabled (staging tested).

Bonsai watchlist (signals and thresholds):
- Latency:
  - route:/v1/generate-high p50 delta >= +20% from baseline (30m sustained) -> ALERT
  - route:/v1/generate-high p95 delta >= +15% (10m burst) -> HIGH ALERT
- Error/fallback rate:
  - fallback-rate (tokenization fallback) > 0.5% absolute increase (10m) -> ALERT
  - 5xx rate > baseline +0.2% (5m) -> ALERT
- Quality proxies:
  - Eval-set A BLEU-like metric drop >= 6 points (hourly sample of 200 prompts) -> INVESTIGATE
  - Unexpected decode patterns (restarts, truncated outputs) > 0.1% -> INVESTIGATE
- Cost metrics:
  - cost-per-token increase > 10% (60m) -> REVIEW
- Cache health:
  - KV hit-rate drop > 5% sustained (30m) -> INVESTIGATE

Signal owners (first responder):
- Latency/5xx: Daniel Kim (SRE)
- Eval-quality regressions: Marta Lopez (Applied ML)
- Cost deltas and billing: Sean O'Neill (Infra-econ)
- KV cache issues: Aisha Patel (Runtime)

Rapid response playbook (first 30 minutes):
- Step 0: If any HIGH ALERT fires (p95 +15% or 5xx spike), paging goes out to primary SRE.
- Step 1: Triage channel: open #canary-triage-{canary-id} (autocreated), post baseline vs current digests (link to graph snapshots).
- Step 2: Quick hypothesis checklist: code path mismatch? kernel selection change? quantization profile change? routing policy drift?
- Step 3: If latency regression confirmed across >2 regions or persistent for 30m, flip canary traffic back to stable via routing policy (automated knob: rollback-route canary->stable).
- Step 4: Run targeted smoke test on the canary instance (local replay of 50 representative sessions) and attach logs.
- Step 5: If unresolved after 60m, escalate to on-call manager and prepare rollback notes for postmortem.

Rollback triggers (automated + manual):
Automated triggers (immediate rollback):
- 5xx rate > baseline +1% sustained for 5m.
- p95 latency +30% sustained for 10m.
- Error classification: model decode failure (tokenizer crashes) > 0.2%.

Manual triggers (require two approvals: SRE + Runtime owner):
- Cost-per-token increase > 20% and still climbing after 2h.
- Quality regression detected on eval-set A with BLEU-like drop >10 points.

Hourly calendar (T-0 to T+36h):
- T-6h: Final release sync: confirm knobs, confirm canary cohort, confirm alerting dashboards.
- T-2h: Preflight roll call: make sure on-call Slack pings were acknowledged.
- T-30m: Abort window check: if any unresolved critical PRs exist, abort.
- T+0: Flip 1% traffic to canary. Run 0–10 minute smoke checks.
- T+15m: Ops check-in (5m): p50/p95 snapshot.
- T+45m: Full telemetry snapshot (10m): compare against baseline.
- T+90m: Decision gate — continue to 1% for 24h or rollback.
- T+24h: If stable, raise to 5% traffic for 12h.
- T+36h: If stable at 5% for 12h, schedule a controlled ramp (separate doc) and notify product/CS for customer-facing notes.

Comms recipe (internal and customer):
- Internal blurb (post to #release-ops): 1–2 sentences and a link to canary-triage and graphs. Example: "Canary v3a running at 1% on region-us-east; no critical signals at T+1h — continuing 24h window. Triage: <link>."
- On-call escalation: page policy is: P1 -> immediate page both primary and backup, P2 -> Slack ping.
- External customer-facing blurb (if we need to notify customers): keep it focused, e.g., "We are running a short canary for runtime improvements; you might see transient latency variation in US region during the window. No action required. Contact support if you see >3% request errors."

Quick notes for release notes (draft snippet to reuse):
- Runtime patch v3a (canary): Improves KV cache predictability for short-head prompt patterns and stabilizes kernel dispatch for small-batch scenarios. Rolling canary starting 2026-03-15. We will monitor latency, cost-per-token and fallbacks.

Post-window checklist (T+36h):
- [ ] Collate canary telemetry and attach to PR (s3 export).
- [ ] Fill the postmortem template if any trigger fired (use the short PM template below).
- [ ] Retrospective: Was the Bonsai watchlist adequate? Add/subtract signals as needed.
- [ ] Tag follow-up engineering tasks and assign owners (e.g., quant-profile adjustments, kernel patch roll-forward).

Short PM template (if triggered):
- What happened (one-paragraph summary)
- Impact (routes affected, percent of traffic, customer-visible errors)
- Root cause (hypothesis + evidence)
- Timeline (T-6h to T+end)
- Mitigation + rollback steps taken
- Long-term actions (owner + due date)

Open items / TODOs (owner):
- (Aisha) finalize smoke-suite additions to include the small-batch kernel path tests (due 2026-03-08).
- (Daniel) add a derived metric for "eval quality delta" into dashboard (due 2026-03-09).
- (Marta) confirm the eval-set A run is reproducible and add seeding notes to PR (due 2026-03-07).
- (Sean) pre-authorize cost telemetry access for the on-call (due 2026-03-10).

Notes to self:
- Keep the Bonsai list intentionally short; adding too many noisy metrics masks signal. If we see false positives, tighten thresholds rather than adding more metrics.
- Keep comms short; after-action notes should contain links to graphs and the S3 telemetry snapshot only.

Appendix: quick links and dashboards
- Latency dashboard: https://kibana.redwood/oss/latency?panel=canary
- Canary triage channel template: https://confluence.redwood/triage-templates#canary
- Baseline S3 snapshot: s3://redwood-rollouts/baselines/2026-03-canary.json
- Canary-run PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/998

End of dossier.
